knowledge:
- key_parameters: inp=The input object for corral, which can be a matrix, SingleCellExperiment, or SummarizedExperiment ;; splitby=A character string specifying the colData attribute that tracks batches/platforms in corralm or sce2matlist ;; whichmat=Character string specifying which assay matrix to use, defaulting to 'counts' ;; fullout=Logical; if TRUE, corral returns the full list output (SVD, coordinates) instead of just the SingleCellExperiment with the reducedDim slot ;; rtype=Residual type to decompose; 'standardized'/'pearson' (default) or 'freemantukey' (more robust to overdispersion) ;; vst_mth=Variance stabilizing transformation method; options include 'sqrt', 'anscombe', and 'freemantukey' ;; powdef_alpha=Numeric power of alpha in (0,1) for power deflation smoothing of residuals; defaults to NULL ;; smooth=Logical; if TRUE, applies alternative smoothing by symmetrically trimming extreme values ;; pct_trim=Fraction of extreme values to trim when smooth=TRUE; defaults to 0.01
- alternatives: PCA=Mentioned as designed for continuous, approximately normally distributed data, whereas CA is designed for non-negative count-based data on the same additive scale
- when_to_use: Use corral for dimensionality reduction of single-cell count data to address high dimensionality and sparsity. Use corralm for multi-table batch alignment and integration across different platforms or batches of single-cell data.
- pitfalls: Standard CA is sensitive to rare objects or outlier cells which can exert undue influence on a dimension; this can be mitigated using rtype='freemantukey', vst_mth, powdef_alpha, or smooth=TRUE. For corralm, input matrices must be matched by features (genes) before running. Scaled variance (scal_var) assumes the types of cells represented in different datasets are expected to be similar and cannot account for fundamentally different cell type distributions between batches. SVD axis directions can flip between runs due to fast approximation with irlba.

workflows.name: single_dataset_dimension_reduction
workflows.intent: Perform correspondence analysis (CA) for dimensionality reduction on a single single-cell dataset.
workflows.stages: 1. Run corral on the SingleCellExperiment specifying the count assay ;; 2. Visualize the embedding using plot_embedding_sce ;; 3. Run downstream visualization like UMAP or tSNE using scater on the corral reduced dimension ;; 4. Run corral on a raw count matrix to get coordinates and SVD output ;; 5. Generate a biplot using biplot_corral to visualize links between features and cells
workflows.code:
zm4eq.sce <- corral(inp = zm4eq.sce, 
                    whichmat = 'counts')

plot_embedding_sce(sce = zm4eq.sce,
                   which_embedding = 'corral',
                   plot_title = 'corral on Zhengmix4eq',
                   color_attr = 'phenoid',
                   color_title = 'cell type',
                   saveplot = FALSE)

zm4eq.sce <- runUMAP(zm4eq.sce,
                     dimred = 'corral',
                     name = 'corral_UMAP')
zm4eq.sce <- runTSNE(zm4eq.sce,
                     dimred = 'corral',
                     name = 'corral_TSNE')

ggplot_umap <- plot_embedding_sce(sce = zm4eq.sce,
                                  which_embedding = 'corral_UMAP',
                                  plot_title = 'Zhengmix4eq corral with UMAP',
                                  color_attr = 'phenoid',
                                  color_title = 'cell type',
                                  returngg = TRUE,
                                  showplot = FALSE,
                                  saveplot = FALSE)

ggplot_tsne <- plot_embedding_sce(sce = zm4eq.sce,
                                  which_embedding = 'corral_TSNE',
                                  plot_title = 'Zhengmix4eq corral with tSNE',
                                  color_attr = 'phenoid',
                                  color_title = 'cell type',
                                  returngg = TRUE,
                                  showplot = FALSE,
                                  saveplot = FALSE)

gridExtra::grid.arrange(ggplot_umap, ggplot_tsne, ncol = 2)

zm4eq.countmat <- assay(zm4eq.sce,'counts')
zm4eq.countcorral <- corral(zm4eq.countmat)

celltype_vec <- zm4eq.sce$phenoid
plot_embedding(embedding = zm4eq.countcorral$v,
               plot_title = 'corral on Zhengmix4eq',
               color_vec = celltype_vec,
               color_title = 'cell type',
               saveplot = FALSE)

gene_names <- rowData(zm4eq.sce)$symbol

biplot_corral(corral_obj = zm4eq.countcorral, color_vec = celltype_vec, text_vec = gene_names)

workflows.name: multi_batch_integration
workflows.intent: Align and integrate single-cell datasets from different batches or platforms using corralm.
input: scmix_sce (SingleCellExperiment with a batch/platform covariate in colData)
workflows.stages: 1. Run corralm on the SingleCellExperiment specifying the batch covariate in splitby ;; 2. Visualize the integrated embedding using plot_embedding_sce ;; 3. Convert to a list of matrices using sce2matlist and run corralm on the list ;; 4. Evaluate batch integration using the scaled variance metric with scal_var
workflows.code:
scmix_sce <- corralm(scmix_sce, splitby = 'Method')

plot_embedding_sce(sce = scmix_sce, 
                   which_embedding = 'corralm', 
                   color_attr = 'Method', 
                   color_title = 'platform', 
                   ellipse_attr = 'cell_line', 
                   plot_title = 'corralm on scmix', 
                   saveplot = FALSE)

scmix_matlist <- sce2matlist(sce = scmix_sce, 
                             splitby = 'Method', 
                             whichmat = 'counts')

scmix_corralm <- corralm(scmix_matlist)

plot_embedding(embedding = scmix_corralm$v, 
               plot_title = 'corralm on scmix', 
               color_vec = platforms, 
               color_title = 'platform', 
               ellipse_vec = cell_lines, 
               saveplot = FALSE)

scal_var(scmix_corralm)
